text.tspan: AutoDesign
Meta-Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Agentic Design
Yaxin Luo*, Haobin Jiang*, Jialv Zou, Xu Huang, Wenhao Yan, Haodong Li, Zhengrong Yue, Jing Li, Xiaofu Chen, Xiaohan Zhao, Jiacheng Liu, Jiacheng Cui, Zhiqiang Shen, Xiaotong Li
Meituan · MBZUAI · Huazhong University of Science and Technology · Peking University · Tsinghua University · The Chinese University of Hong Kong · Shanghai Jiao Tong University
Improve the harness. Keep the model fixed.
Why optimize the harness?
Scientific design takes more than a single generation. An
agent must understand the paper, select evidence, write
layout code and repair the rendered result. Static
workflows repeat the same failures. AutoDesign turns the
surrounding harness into an optimization target, using
human-annotated reference artifacts and optional
natural-language guidance to ground design preferences.
Input, model and output

tspan.tspan: a paper PDF, its figures and tables, and design

text.tspan: constraints. A fixed LLM or MLLM works inside the
harness. The inner loop outputs an editable artifact and its
execution trajectory. Across tasks, the meta-harness
outputs an improved DesignHarness. Model weights remain
unchanged.
How PosterBench judges quality
The Main Track contains 100 papers across five
disciplines. PosterBench-mini is a shared 10-paper
subset for controlled comparisons. The frozen external
benchmark is separate from the evaluator used during
harness optimization. Seven weighted dimensions
assess source truth, scientific communication and
rendered usability. Severe failures impose score ceilings.
Faithfulness 10 · Coverage 10 · Density 15
Visual evidence 10 · Layout 20
Readability 25 · Aesthetics 10
Key methods of AutoDesign
Improve the artifact.
The designer writes or revises
the current artifact. A rule validator checks layout and
source integrity, while a visual critic reviews the
rendered design. Their feedback guides localized
revision. Within this loop, the harness stays fixed.
Improve the harness.
Training tasks produce artifacts,
trajectories and quality scores. The optimizer reads this
evidence and the persistent history, identifies recurrent
failures, proposes a plan and edits exactly one harness
component. Its five options are context and memory,
tools and specifications, execution runtime,
orchestration, or evaluation and feedback. The evaluator
is initialized from human-annotated references and stays
fixed during autonomous optimization. Revising it
requires explicit human guidance.
Accept only transferable gains.
Promote the
candidate only if training quality improves and
development quality does not decline. Otherwise retain
the old harness. Development traces and scores stay
outside the proposer and its memory. Accepted and
rejected training-side updates remain available for
comparison and rollback.
Method: Meta-Harness Optimization (Overview)
From a paper to an editable poster
Source ingestion preserves metadata, figures and evidence locations. The designer authors editable HTML and the rule validator
checks each attempt. Failed blocking checks trigger visual critique and localized revision. This implementation permits up to 12
attempts, then applies history-based fallback under integrity constraints if needed. Finalization renders and prepares the selected
candidate for delivery.

Human preference
Eleven reviewers supplied 933 valid system-blind ranking judgments.

tspan.tspan: AutoDesign has the highest Bradley–Terry estimate:

text.tspan: alternative. This estimate is not a raw win rate.
Scope and open questions
Formal evaluation covers academic posters. Slides, webpages and
videos remain pilot outputs. Better component selection and evaluator
evolution are still open research problems. Extending the system
requires medium-specific data, objectives, rendering checks and
human validation.
